lessons.title: The conversation crosses a short list of systems
lessons.summary: Carrier, trunk or Edge, Architect, queue, agent, then the systems beside the agent.
paras: A voice conversation enters through Genesys Cloud Voice or BYOC, optionally through a premises Edge, and reaches Architect. Architect transfers to a queue. ACD offers an agent who is On Queue and under utilization. Recording, quality, workforce management, speech analytics, Copilot, and a CRM sit beside that path. They can fail alone. The topology studio is the picture, with failure toggles that drop one link at a time.

Digital conversations skip the trunk and still use Architect, queues, and the same beside-the-agent systems when those products are in the package. CX 1 is voice. Digital and quality arrive at CX 2. WEM and transcription minutes arrive at CX 3. Copilot arrives at CX 4. The overview is the stack.

lessons.title: WFM, QM, E911, analytics, CRM, and bots are sisters
lessons.summary: Each sister has a track and a page. None of them is a setting on the queue tab alone.
paras: Workforce management is business units, schedules, and adherence, inside WEM, on CX 3. Quality is forms, policies, and coaching, from CX 2. Emergency calling is a classification, a route, and a location, with BYOC leaving you responsible for the provider. STA is transcription and topics. Bots and Copilot are the AI track. CRM is AppFoundry plus the Salesforce and Zendesk articles.
The glossary in this lab is a short restatement of those pages, each with a link. If the glossary and the page disagree, the page wins. The glossary is not a second source of truth.

Specialists are listed by name: Architect, Workforce Management, Scripting, Quality Management, Outbound, and Speech and Text Analytics. lessons.title: What this lab will not invent
lessons.summary: Prices, unconfirmed hosts, exam codes, lifecycle dates, and CRM feature lists stay off the page.
paras: The rules that built the lessons: cite a page that was actually opened, prefer Genesys articles and the RFCs for SIP, RTP, SRTP, and DTMF, use documentation addresses from RFC 5737 in synthetic logs, and mark uncertainty when a number can move. Fair-use dollar figures, DCVP IP lists, dialect lists, and country-by-country voice coverage are links, not copies.

Specialist exams are names. Implicit grant’s date is the OAuth article’s date. PureConnect and Engage dates wait for a Genesys notice. Dynamics and ServiceNow wait for a listing. Webex waits for a document you attach. If a later page disagrees with a lesson, the page wins, and the lesson should be read as the way to find that page.
lessons.uncertainty: If you find a lesson that states a price, a DCVP prefix, a GCX- code, or a PureConnect end date, treat that sentence as a bug.

lessons.title: The telephony door this lab can cite is BYOC, not a word the page did not use
lessons.summary: CPaaS is the classroom name for a communications API you bring. The opened page is About BYOC Cloud.
paras: About BYOC Cloud says the solution lets you define SIP trunks between the Genesys Cloud AWS-based Edge and Media Tier and a third-party carrier over the public internet. That is the door this lab will teach when someone asks for a communications-platform bridge: your carrier, Genesys media, and the articles for trunks, number plans, ports, and emergency calling. The page does not use the word CPaaS. This lesson will not add it to the product.

BYOC Premises is the other door, with a customer Edge, and it has its own track. Genesys Cloud Voice is the Genesys carrier offer and stays on the voice-region article. AppFoundry lists a Telco and Devices category among others. A listing there is not a configuration this lab performed. The Developer Center is where a client would be written, and this lab’s API explorer still does not send one.

lessons.title: Salesforce and Zendesk are the embeds this lab opened
lessons.summary: Salesforce Open CTI is in maintenance and has a later retirement date. Zendesk’s page does not say that.
paras: About Genesys Cloud for Salesforce describes the embed inside Salesforce and says that, effective 23 March 2026, the integration is deprecated, in maintenance, and will not receive new features. The deprecation article opened beside it is a different sentence: announced 23 March 2026, planned effective date 28 February 2028, when Salesforce retires Open CTI and this integration retires with it. That announcement says there is no immediate impact, and it names two paths: CX Cloud from Genesys and Salesforce, or the Genesys Cloud user interface with no Salesforce CTI. It also says the two can run side by side, and that a migration’s length varies.

About Genesys Cloud for Zendesk describes the embed inside Zendesk, with nothing to install on each computer, and lists support for call, callback, outbound dialing, email, message, and ACD voicemail. Both articles say not to run different embedded clients, including Salesforce and Zendesk, at the same time. Both mention Agent Copilot in the interaction window. Other CRMs stay on AppFoundry until you open a listing. This lab did not install either embed.
lessons.uncertainty: Read in 2026-10. The about page says maintenance effective 23 March 2026. The deprecation table says planned retirement 28 February 2028. The announcement says migration length varies and does not give one duration for every customer.

lessons.title: A bot, a Virtual Agent, and Copilot are three assists
lessons.summary: Dialog Engine builds the bot. Virtual Agent adds Genesys AI. Copilot sits with the person.
paras: About Genesys Dialog Engine Bot Flows says you build bots in Architect and use them in call, chat, and message flows. The page says the feature is PCI DSS-compliant and can be used in secure call flows. It also points at Genesys Virtual Agent: an advanced conversational bot for voice and digital bot flows that can generate intents and utterances, search knowledge-base content on digital interactions, and summarize the bot conversation with a wrap-up code. Token metering has its own article. This lesson does not copy a price.

Agent Copilot, on its overview, assists a person during and after the interaction: knowledge articles, a transcript, scripts, next best action, a form, and notes that can include the reason, the resolution, and a possible wrap-up code. The overview says the benefit continues when an agent blind-transfers a call or a digital interaction. Copilot is not the bot that answered first, and Virtual Agent is not the panel on the human agent’s screen. The Salesforce and Zendesk articles both say Copilot can be placed in the embedded interaction window.

lessons.title: Future hooks are dates on announcements, not a roadmap this lab invented
lessons.summary: Journey Outcomes, Salesforce Open CTI, and Customer Outcomes are three different sentences.
paras: The Journey Outcomes announcement lists announced-on 18 May 2026 and planned effective date 29 June 2026. After that date the page says outcomes cannot be created, existing outcomes are not processed, action maps are not triggered by them, and reporting for them is not available. Customer Outcomes is described there as under development, and Outcome Scoring is not part of it. Architect flows that call getJourneyOutcome skip that branch. This lab did not sign in to see whether a given org still has the feature.

The Salesforce Open CTI announcement is the other dated hook: announced 23 March 2026, planned effective 28 February 2028, with no immediate impact stated on that page. The predictive-routing custom-KPI announcement is a third page, and the predictive track is where this lab keeps it. A future hook in a design should name the announcement, the date printed on it, and the sentence “re-open before you rely.” A hook without that page is a guess.
lessons.uncertainty: Checked in 2026-10. This lab did not sign in to an organization, so it cannot say whether Journey Outcomes is still present in any given org.
